sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 of the Sanborn Audubon series of August 1930, covering part of Haddon Township, Camden County, east of the Borough of Oaklyn. The township and borough line is drawn down East Clinton Avenue on the west and along North White Horse Pike on the south; north is towards the upper left. The part shows eight parallel avenues, East Clinton, East Collingswood, East Greenwood, East Oakland, Ormond, East Holly, East Park and East Cedar, running from the pike north-east across Johnson Avenue towards Cold Springs Avenue and a diagonal back line of lots. Newton Lake curves across the top of the sheet, and Oaklawn Avenue meets East Clinton Avenue at its north-west corner. The blocks are almost entirely detached one- and two-storey frame dwellings with small garages on narrow lots, many still vacant, with lot subdivisions drawn north of Cold Springs Avenue. Commerce is confined to a row of brick and concrete-block stores fronting North White Horse Pike, among them a bake shop and the Ritz Theatre (movies, with a stage) between Ormond and East Holly Avenues. The Emmanuel M.E. Church stands on East Cedar Avenue south of Johnson Avenue, and a golf course occupies the block between East Holly and East Park Avenues at the pike. Six-inch water pipes run along the avenues and the pike, with hydrants marked. The blocks east of East Cedar Avenue (sheet 6), west of the Oaklyn line (sheet 4) and south of the pike (sheets 11 and 12) are left blank except for street outlines. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Cold Springs Avenue is Coldsprings Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
The pike's junctions are named White Horse Pike in OpenStreetMap at these avenues.
The Oaklawn Avenue and East Cedar Avenue / Johnson Avenue junctions were hand-picked; the detector did not find them.
Below the pike the sheet shows the ends of West Collingswood, West Greenwood, West Oakland (lettered W. Oaland Av.), West Holly and West Park Avenues, outside the mask.
Ritz Theatre (movies) and a row of stores on North White Horse Pike; Emmanuel M.E. Church on East Cedar Avenue; a golf course at East Holly and East Park Avenues.

Printed sheet 5 of the Audubon series (Aug. 1930), Haddon Township east of the Borough of Oaklyn line. Scale 100 ft to an inch; north to the upper left (fitted rotation about -57 deg). One part: E. Clinton to E. Cedar Av. between N. White Horse Pike and Cold Springs Av./Newton Lake. Stubs of the W. avenues south of the pike (sheets 11, 12) are outside the mask.
